subject.title: [Bug]: /context detail shows ~62k untracked provider/runtime overhead on fresh OpenAI Codex gpt-5.5 session

question: What public semantics should `/context detail` use for Codex app-server token usage: active context-window occupancy, provider billing totals, provider-reported native thread state, or a multi-bucket ledger with confidence levels?
rationale: Current code can expose a delta, and Codex exposes both total and last usage, but choosing bucket names and whether they influence compaction is a user-visible product contract that source inspection alone cannot settle.

options.title: Ship a multi-bucket ledger
options.body: Separate context-window, billing/cache, tracked prompt, compactable transcript, provider/native, and unknown buckets, and require live Codex proof before updating semantics.

options.title: Keep generic overhead for now
options.body: Leave the issue open as a known diagnostic limitation until a narrower live Codex proof path is available.

options.title: Treat the Codex value as active context only
options.body: Relabel the current delta around last-turn usage, accepting the risk that billing/cache/provider state may still be misrepresented.

recommendation.title: Ship a multi-bucket ledger
recommendation.body: Separate context-window, billing/cache, tracked prompt, compactable transcript, provider/native, and unknown buckets, and require live Codex proof before updating semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current partial context-detail diagnostic improvement and are closest to the report surface that needs the product decision.
